papers.title: Processing-dependent mechanical response and mesoscale heterogeneity of diammonium phosphate-modified API Class G oilwell cement
papers.abstract: Diammonium phosphate (DAP) can modify cement hydration, but its effects on hardened mechanical behavior, elastic response, and structural uniformity during elevated-temperature curing remain insufficiently understood. This study investigated API Class G oilwell cement containing 0.25-1.00% DAP by weight of cement (BWOC), cured at 85 °C under atmospheric pressure. A dual-track design evaluated thermally conditioned slurries (Track A) and slurries cast without pre-casting conditioning (Track B). Characterization comprised unconfined compressive strength (UCS), scratch testing, ultrasonic pulse velocity, and X-ray computed tomography (CT). In Track A, 0.25-0.50% DAP enhanced mean UCS, reaching 54.5 MPa at 14 days for 0.50% DAP versus 48.4 MPa for neat cement. In Track B, mean UCS decreased with dosage at every age, whereas between-specimen UCS standard deviations showed no consistent dosage trend. Mean scratch-derived strength was non-monotonic; however, the age-averaged scratch-response standard deviation increased from 3.00 MPa for neat cement to 7.70 MPa for 1.00% DAP. Nominal dynamic Young’s modulus, calculated using a common reference density, also decreased with dosage. An endpoint CT comparison (n = 1 per formulation) suggested greater mesoscale density variability in the scanned 1.00% DAP specimen than in the scanned neat cement specimen (113.42 versus 86.45 mean slice standard deviation). The results identify protocol-specific and dosage-dependent responses. Moderate DAP improved mean strength under Track A conditions, whereas Track B showed lower mean strength and nominal dynamic stiffness with dosage, together with greater age-averaged scratch-response variability. These findings support combining strength, elastic, and spatial-variability measurements when evaluating DAP-modified oilwell cement under the investigated conditions.

papers.title: A hybrid machine learning–physics framework for predicting electronic properties of Mg-doped bulk and two-dimensional ZnO in data-sparse regimes
papers.abstract: Predicting composition-dependent properties of doped semiconductors remains challenging due to data scarcity and the band-gap underestimation associated with standard density functional theory (DFT). In this work, a hybrid machine-learning (ML) and physics-informed framework is developed for Mg-doped bulk and two-dimensional ZnO. A Gradient Boosting Regressor is used for band-gap prediction, and an empirical post-processing calibration of approximately 1.4 eV is applied to bring the PBE-derived predictions closer to the experimental band-gap scale. Particular attention is given to the low-doping regime, where training data are sparse. Composition-dependent bowing coefficients were first calculated using the ZnO and MgO band-gap endpoints and the corresponding alloy band gaps. A quadratic fit was then extrapolated into the low-doping region, yielding a representative bowing coefficient of approximately 4.9 eV around 5 at% Mg. This value was held fixed for the final 0–12 at% Mg band-gap calculations and combined with the calibrated ML output through a composition-dependent weighting scheme. Without bowing correction, the calibrated ML predictions show a slight band-gap increase in bulk ZnO, whereas the band gap of two-dimensional ZnO remains nearly constant at low Mg concentrations before decreasing at higher concentrations. After applying the bowing-based correction, the low-doping predictions show a clearer band-gap increase and reasonable agreement with reported experimental values. Formation energy exhibits a non-monotonic dependence on Mg concentration. The proposed framework provides a computationally efficient approach for composition-dependent prediction in data-limited doped semiconductors.

summary_en.motivation: Composition-dependent property prediction for doped semiconductors is hampered by sparse data and the systematic band-gap underestimation of standard DFT.
summary_en.method: A gradient boosting regressor with empirical band-gap calibration and a composition-dependent bowing correction is applied to Mg-doped bulk and two-dimensional ZnO.
summary_en.result: The calibrated and bowing-corrected predictions reproduce the experimentally reported band-gap increase in the low-doping regime and reveal a non-monotonic formation-energy trend.
summary_en.validation: Predictions are compared against previously reported experimental band-gap values.
